captions.instagram:
How is ice cream made?

A scoop of ice cream is half air. The rest is millions of ice crystals, tiny balls of fat and a syrup that never freezes. Pull a scoop apart, chill a pot with salt and ice, spin the scraper blades, whip in the air, design your own scoop, and see why kulfi melts slowly and a thawed tub turns icy.

→ A scoop of ice cream is four things at once: ice crystals, air bubbles, fat globules and a syrup that never freezes.
→ By volume it is about half air, a quarter ice, a twentieth fat, and the rest sweet liquid syrup.
→ Sweet mix only starts to freeze at about −2.6 °C, so plain ice at 0 °C can never freeze it.
→ Salt makes the ice melt, and melting takes heat: the pot chills itself towards −21 °C and the mix freezes.
→ Blades scrape ice off a wall at −30 °C, scattering millions of tiny crystals smaller than 50 micrometres.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/icecreamclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How is ice cream made? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
A scoop of ice cream is half air. The rest is millions of ice crystals, tiny balls of fat and a syrup that never freezes. Pull a scoop apart, chill a pot with salt and ice, spin the scraper blades, whip in the air, design your own scoop, and see why kulfi melts slowly and a thawed tub turns icy.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/icecreamclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/icecreamclear

In this video:
• A scoop is four things at once. Under a microscope, ice cream is ice crystals about 50 micrometres across, air bubbles a little bigger, fat globules about 1 micrometre across, and a thick sugar syrup that is still liquid.
• Salt makes ice colder than ice. Sweet mix only starts to freeze at about −2.6 °C, so plain ice at 0 °C can never freeze it.
• Freeze fast and scrape the wall. Big crystals feel icy: the tongue notices them above about 50 micrometres.
• Half of it is air. The dasher whips air in as it scrapes.
• Sugar is the antifreeze. Sugar lowers the freezing point, and as ice forms the syrup left behind gets stronger.
• Kulfi, gelato and the refreeze problem. Kulfi is thick, slow-boiled milk frozen without churning, so it holds almost no air and melts slowly.
